ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.
5.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
July 1, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday, July 1,
2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were Assistant City
Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse, Community Services
Director McPherron, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Parks and Recreation Director
Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Traina seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

3. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that Eshelman Project for water replacement
and street resurfacing went for bid and the bid opening will be on July 22, 2013.

According to City Manager Rock, the City received three bids for Lomita and Crenshaw
Construction Project, and the lowest bidder was American Asphalt (project cost - $928,000.)

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Gazeley invited those in attendance to the IRWU Second Texas Holdem Poker
Tournament on July 30, 2013, at 6pm at Normandie Casino with the benefits being donated for
a childhood cancer research.  Councilmember Gazeley announced that South Bay
Environmental Services Department is sponsoring Kids Health and Fun Fair at St. Margaret
Church on July 6, 2013, from 9 am to 1pm. Councilmember Gazeley reported that the League
of California Cities asking cities to support AB 1147 regarding massage therapy establishments
that would allow cities to issue revocable certificates of registration for the owners.

  Page 1
 Councilmember Gazeley informed those in attendance that five dead crows were found in
Lomita and warned residents to take precautions regarding West Nile Virus. Councilmember
Gazeley requested future agenda item to discuss City’s potential participation in HERO program
that would allow Lomita residents energy efficient improvements for their residencies.
Councilmember Gazeley added that the program is currently administered by SBCCOG. All
Councilmembers agreed to place this item on the future agenda.

Councilmember Savidan stated that Mayor Estrada and himself attended Alice Abbot’s
retirement luncheon. Councilmember Savidan wished the best to the new Water Treatment
Operator who was recently hired.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, urged City Council to reconsider Oversized Vehicle Ordinance
and make more changes including having distinction between commercial and residential
vehicles, requiring permit for parking on the weekends, and include markings such as mirrors,
ladders, roof racks into the three dimension requirements for the vehicle size.

Marty Spain, Lomita resident, asked the City staff to schedule properly street sweeping and
trash removal as it happens usually at the same time during the holidays.

Michael Pucci, Keizer Permanente Representative and Lomita Chamber of Commerce Member,
invited those in attendance to the Chamber’s next Business Networking Mixer, which will take
place at Community Child on July 25, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.

6. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez requested to pull item 6.E. Councilmember Traina moved to approve
the Consent Agenda minus item 6.E. Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion, which
carried unanimously.

Councilmember Sanchez asked about the nature of 95 code enforcement cases as reported in
the Community Development Department monthly report and what the procedure of resolving
the cases, to which Assistant City Manager Sugano responded that it all depends on the nature
of the case, staff contacts the business owner or residents by phone or by sending a letter. If it
escalates beyond warning, the case is assigned to the City Attorney. Discussion followed of
when proactive code enforcement program started and what it involves. Councilmember Traina
asked to provide detailed list of the code enforcement cases.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve Item 6.E. Councilmember Traina seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  a. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on
  June 17, 2013, and the Regular City Council meeting held on June 17, 2013.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  b. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  Page 2
   c. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  d. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. May 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. Approval of an Ordinance amending various sections of the Lomita Municipal Code
  establishing definitions, designating use, and adopting planning and approval requirements
  for emergency shelters, transitional and supportive housing, and single room occupancy
  units. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  j. Consider authorizing the Mayor to sign a letter of support for Assembly Bill 576 relative to
  state tax revenue and establishment of a Revenue Recovery and Collaborative
  Enforcement Team (RRACE).

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

7.  COMMISSIONER APPOINTMENT (PLANNING COMMISSION)

Councilmembers Savidan, Gazeley, and Mayor Estrada nominated Gia Stokes to fill the vacancy
on the Planning Commission.

Gia Stokes was appointed to the Planning Commission.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:22 p.m in memory of Barbara Angelich, Jose Reynaldo Paz, Verdis Bible
and Kenneth Leroy "Joe" Rowell.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
